definitions.explanation: Humble term used when referring to one's own older brother when speaking to others outside the family.

examples.japanese: {兄|あに}は{大学生|だいがくせい}です。
examples.english: My older brother is a university student.

examples.japanese: {兄|あに}は{東京|とうきょう}に{住|す}んでいます。
examples.english: My older brother lives in Tokyo.

examples.japanese: {兄|あに}は3{歳|さい}{年上|としうえ}です。
examples.english: My older brother is 3 years older.

examples.japanese: {兄|あに}は{結婚|けっこん}していて、{子供|こども}が{二人|ふたり}います。
examples.english: My older brother is married and has two children.

examples.japanese: {兄|あに}は{医者|いしゃ}になりたくて、{毎日|まいにち}{遅|おそ}くまで{勉強|べんきょう}しています。
examples.english: My older brother wants to become a doctor, so he studies late every day.

notes:
{兄|あに} is the humble term for one's own older brother, used when speaking to people outside the family.

FAMILY TERM SYSTEM:
- {兄|あに}: my older brother (humble, to outsiders)
- お{兄|にい}さん: older brother (polite, someone else's or direct address)
- お{兄|にい}ちゃん: big bro (casual, within family)
- {兄貴|あにき}: big brother (masculine/informal)

USAGE NOTES:
Within the family, children often call their older brother お{兄|にい}ちゃん or by name. {兄|あに} is specifically for describing your brother to others.

RELATED FAMILY TERMS:
- {姉|あね}: my older sister (humble)
- {弟|おとうと}: my younger brother (humble)
- {妹|いもうと}: my younger sister (humble)

The pattern is consistent: plain forms for your own family, お〜さん for others' or polite address.
